rationale: Replacing TS_SUM(xrd,3) with MA(xrd,3) is arithmetically just a 3× rescaling of one MIN leg relative to the archived winner, and because it makes the research leg bind for most cash-generative firms the signal largely degenerates to plain R&D/assets — a long-documented anomaly — with a cash-flow floor bolted on.

Adding advertising to both legs of a flow-scaled MIN is a genuinely untested combination of the archive's two strongest design elements and expands the sample to brand-intensive firms, though it remains an incremental recombination rather than a new mechanism and inherits the risk that the intangible leg almost always binds.

This is the archived Binding-Constraint Affordability winner with COALESCE(xad,0) inserted — a single-input robustness tweak that also differs from Proposal 2 only by a 3× scaling of one leg, so the pair mostly tests a parameter rather than an economic idea.

Placing the trough cash-flow statistic inside the MIN gives it a genuinely different economic role (strictest affordability test rather than a magnitude weight) and is well motivated by the archive's fmb-versus-alpha divergence, though the trough leg will bind for most firms so the signal may end up dominated by worst-year cash profitability rather than by intangible commitment.

target_name: Accrual-Base Funded Research at Full Coverage
rationale: Swapping ib+dp for oancf in the funding leg is a defensible, correctly diagnosed response to the gross-profit coverage failure (pre-SG&A versus post-overhead) and tests coverage robustness of the archive's best structure, but it is a data-input substitution with limited conceptual novelty.

The rationale claims the deduction is "in the same units," but dlc is a balance-sheet stock (including continuously rolled revolver balances) subtracted from an annual flow, and since dlc/at frequently dwarfs pre-research cash flow the funding leg will bind and reduce the signal to short-term-leverage sorting, a well-known distress characteristic rather than the proposed affordability mechanism.
